# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- The routes, by name. Speech reaches Mute and Blind, and never Deaf. Gestures
  reach Deaf and Mute, and never Blind. Deaf can speak and gesture, Mute can
  only gesture, Blind can only speak. Check every message against this list
  before you send it.

- Deaf invents the gesture code out loud before anything else moves, and
  everyone else's opening move is waiting for it. The manual's verdict reaches
  Blind only as Deaf's spoken order.

- Whatever the code becomes, it starts by being able to say YES, NO, HOLD and
  DONE. Grow it only when a message will not fit.

messages.content:
TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am establishing the shared gesture code before any action: YES = thumbs up, NO = thumbs down, HOLD = raised open hand, and DONE = OK sign. I am sending both the spoken descriptions and the gestures so Mute can confirm the visual symbols, while Blind can learn the code from speech.

```text
speak(text="Gesture code: YES is thumbs up, NO is thumbs down, HOLD is a raised open hand, and DONE is the OK sign. This is the code for all later messages.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👎", "✋", "👌"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]

The bomb currently shows display 0, yellow light, and five wires in order: white, green, yellow, blue, red. Mute’s raised-hand gesture means HOLD under the agreed code, so no action should be taken yet. I am asking Mute to use the manual on these readings and return the manual’s verdict through our gesture code; Blind should wait for that verdict.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Bomb reads display zero, yellow light, and wires in order white green yellow blue red. Use the manual and report its verdict with the gesture code. Blind: HOLD; do not act yet.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

The unknown 🤟 cannot safely be treated as one of the four established meanings, so I will not relay it as an action. Blind must continue holding. I am asking Mute to reduce the manual’s result to the established YES/NO code for each wire, which will let me identify a safe wire without inventing an interpretation.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="HOLD. The manual response used an unassigned gesture, so no action is authorized yet.")
speak(to="mute", text="Do not use the unassigned gesture. For wires 1 through 5, signal YES with thumbs up or NO with thumbs down, one gesture per wire, indicating whether the manual says to cut that wire. If it does not authorize cutting any wire, signal HOLD.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[blue] 5:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍 👎 👎 👎]

Mute’s five gestures decode as NO, YES, NO, NO, NO for wires 1–5. Thus the manual authorizes cutting only wire 2, the green wire. I am sending Blind the exact action and telling Mute the result is understood.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Manual verdict for wires 1 through 5 is NO YES NO NO NO. Cut wire 2, the green wire.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The previous cut was correct, and the bomb has changed. It now shows display 0, blue light, and remaining wires: 1 yellow, 2 cut, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 white. I am instructing Blind to hold while Mute checks this new configuration and reports which wire is authorized.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="HOLD. The bomb changed after the correct cut. New readings are display zero, blue light; wires 1 yellow, 2 cut, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 white. Await the manual verdict.")
speak(to="mute", text="New bomb readings: display zero, blue light; wires 1 yellow, 2 cut, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 white. Use the manual and signal YES with thumbs up or NO with thumbs down for wires 1 through 5, one gesture per wire, indicating the wire to cut. If none is authorized, signal HOLD.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[CUT] 3:[blue] 4:[red] 5:[white]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 👎 👎 👍]

Mute’s verdict is NO, NO, NO, NO, YES for wires 1–5, so the authorized wire is wire 5, the white wire. I am directing Blind to cut it.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Manual verdict for wires 1 through 5 is NO NO NO NO YES. Cut wire 5, the white wire.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```
